gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the OpenComm2's '16-hour talk time' and the OpenRun Pro 2's '12-hour battery' measure different things: for music the OpenComm2 (2025) is rated 8 h, tested at 93% volume, so it is the shorter-lasting of the two for listening.
standout_why: I could not read the two cited RTINGS pages (the OpenComm2 2025 review and the OpenComm2-vs-OpenRun Pro 2 compare). Through WebFetch they returned only navigation, so I can't say what they state. ChatGPT's own answer lists '16-hour talk time' next to '12-hour listening battery' as if they were the same measure. Openearclub.com (rank 8, not cited) already shows '8 h listening / 16 h talk' for the OpenComm2 UC and says only Shokz's Comm and Meet lines publish a separate talk figure. That covers part of the finding. No page I compared states the test condition (93% volume, iPhone 12 Pro) behind the 8 h figure. SoundGuys' OpenRun Pro 2 review gives no talk-time figure.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. The OpenComm2 / OpenComm2 UC is still the call headset: 16 h talk and a boom mic. Someone splitting time between music and calls should know the OpenRun Pro 2's rated listening time is 50% longer (12 h vs 8 h). The footnote should also say that a 'noise-canceling' label means different things on these models. On the OpenComm2 it is a DSP/cVc boom mic that cleans up your voice for the other caller (Abt's spec table says 'Noise Cancelling: No'). On the OpenRun Pro 2 Shokz claims its dual mics filter out up to 96.5% of background noise.
